decisions.reason: The reference-class electrometer is a flagship that sits at the core of the firm's dosimetry business, so keeping it costs little and its strategic value is clear, which makes abandonment unwarranted.

The oncology risk management software costs little to maintain and supports the patient-safety and convergence direction, and its uptake is still too uncertain two years after launch to justify dropping it.
The CT image quality phantom builds on the firm's established imaging QA offer and carries low holding costs, so this young option should be kept open while its market value resolves.

The mammography phantom is distant from the core business and its value is more uncertain, but it is only a year on the market and cheap to keep listed, so keeping the option open is preferable to early abandonment.

The full field mammography phantom overlaps with Product D and lies outside the core, which makes it the more likely candidate for later consolidation, but it is too early to know its value and holding a physical catalog item costs little.
The medical imaging QA instrument line is a flagship that expands the firm's established offer into imaging, so the firm is committing further rather than abandoning it.
